keep: Use a direct 'password kya hota hai?' question on a specific, named document. 'Aadhaar PDF ka password kya hota hai?' is the top reel at 1971 views, 24 saves and 18 shares. It's also the only top-scoring hook that names a concrete document and a concrete unknown.

Pick topics where the viewer feels an immediate pain: locked PDFs, a file too big to upload, PDF editing, or Aadhaar validity. The top 4 reels are all about these. Saves (24, 13, 4) and shares (18, 7) are highest on them.
Keep hooks short and in plain Hinglish, ideally under 8 words, with the problem stated in the first line. 'PDF ko edit kaise karein?' and 'What if your PDF is too big?' both reached over 1,200 views.

Make a hook that tells viewers the video solves a task. The 'one website for any PDF or photo job' hook got 920 views, and avg watch time stayed at 8.7s. Use this utility framing as a secondary option.
Keep the content tied to Indian document tasks (Aadhaar, PAN, form uploads). This is the account's niche, and all of the best reels sit in it.
avoid: Don't use off-topic or curiosity hooks that don't match the tool. 'Egypt ke tomb mein 3000 saal purana shahad mila' (222 views) and 'Charging 100% tak mat karo' (436 views) have nothing to do with the PDF or photo tools. Both got low shares and saves, so these hooks pull the wrong audience.

Avoid generic how-to or definition hooks for niche sub-topics, such as 'Masked Aadhaar download kaise karte hain?' (3.9s watch, 0 saves) and 'Masked Aadhaar kya hota hai?' (4.6s, 0 saves). The weakest reels all have short watch time (2.2–4.7s) and almost no saves.

Avoid bank-statement, Excel and image-to-PDF topics for now. 'HDFC statement PDF ka password kya hota hai?' (196 and 140 views), 'PDF ka table Excel mein kaise layein?' (123) and 'Photos ko ek PDF kaise banayein?' (116) all got 116–196 views, and none got more than 1 save.

Don't assume the 'secret_answer' format is the cause of success. It appears in both the best and worst reels. The same Aadhaar password hook got 1971 views once and 184 views another time, so the topic and the post itself matter more.

Don't post near-duplicate hooks on the same topic and expect the same result. The two 'Aadhaar print out valid hai?' reels got 463 and 304 views, and the two HDFC password reels got 196 and 140. Repeats come in well below the top performer.
next_tests: Re-run the exact 'Aadhaar PDF ka password kya hota hai?' hook (a repeat got only 184 views) and change one thing at a time. Try a different first-second visual, or a different posting time. This will tell whether the 1971 views came from the hook or from a one-off distribution boost, since the same hook produced 10x fewer views before.

Test the winning 'X ka password kya hota hai?' pattern on other high-demand Indian documents, such as the PAN or ITR PDF and the Aadhaar PDF. 'e-PAN PDF' (290 views) and 'PAN card PDF' (186 views) did poorly, while the bank statement one did worse. Keep the wording identical to isolate the document as the variable.

Run a head-to-head on the 'problem' pain hooks: 'What if your PDF is too big?' compared with a Hinglish version such as 'PDF upload nahi ho raha? File too large?'. The English problem hook got 1323 views, while the Hinglish 'Form ne phir bola File too large' got 245. That could be the language or the topic (compress_pdf vs resize_photo), so change only one.

keep: Lead with a concrete, relatable outcome or person-in-a-situation hook (e.g. 'Can one selfie become an ID photo?', 'Why did Rohan miss his own interview?') — these hold 6–8s average watch time versus 1.7s for the generic 'Any PDF or photo job' hook.
Show a visible before/after of a single task: the selfie-to-ID-photo reel is the best non-manual reel (score 359, 449 views, 397 reach, 2 saves).
Keep stories short and specific to one tool: signature (6.7s watch, 7 shares), Word-to-PDF (8.2s watch) and Ravi's signature (5.8s watch) all held attention better than the multi-tool formats.

Keep the topic tied to a real form or deadline problem (ID photo, signature, interview, KB limits). Saves and shares came from these relatable tasks, but the counts are tiny (1–2 saves, 7 shares at most).

Keep the very short, community-style posts on the list as a separate bucket: the manual hashtag and website posts got the most shares (18) and the second-highest views (352). They are manual posts, so don't treat them as a template for the generated reels.
avoid: Generic umbrella hooks that name no task or person ('Any PDF or photo job – one free website 👇'): 1.7s average watch, the lowest in the set.
Multi-tool cheat-sheet and 'stop paying the cyber cafe' framing: 4.1s watch, 0 shares, and only 147 views despite being 32s long.
Technical-spec openers such as 'Your PDF is 5 MB. The form says 200 KB.' and 'Ravi's signature was 2 MB…': they scored 91–93 with 0 shares and 0 saves.
Question hooks in the secret_answer format (jpg_to_pdf): 0 likes, 0 comments, 0 shares, 0 saves — the question gave no reason to engage.
Reels near or over 30s about spreadsheet or data-entry tasks (bank_statement_excel: 4.8s watch, 113 views, the lowest reach). The format and topic are confounded here, so this is only a weak signal.
next_tests: Re-run the selfie-to-ID-photo before/after format on a second topic (e.g. compress a PDF or resize a signature) with an outcome-led hook and a length under 20s, to see whether before/after drives reach or whether the ID-photo topic did.
Test the same story (e.g. Rohan/Word-to-PDF) with a question hook against a statement hook on an identical body, so the hook effect is isolated from the topic.

Add an explicit end CTA ('Save this for your next form' or 'Send this to a friend filling forms') to the story reels. Saves and shares are near zero everywhere except the manual posts, so this checks whether a prompt changes behaviour.
